$comment: The formatter option surface every runtime must present.
Conformance fixtures pin what the formatters OUTPUT. This pins what they
ACCEPT, which nothing else checks: a Rust builder can grow a field and ship
while Elixir, JavaScript and the CLI silently lack it. Every runtime has a
test that reads this file and fails on a missing option and on a waiver that
`name` is the canonical snake_case option. Each runtime spells it its own
way: Rust and Elixir use it verbatim, JavaScript camelCases it, the CLI
kebab-cases it behind `--`. Where a runtime needs a different spelling,
Adding an option means adding it here first, then watching four runtimes go
red. `waived` is the escape hatch and it can only shrink.
Options a runtime genuinely cannot offer, keyed by runtime then formatter.
Empty, and the tests fail on an entry that is no longer needed, so it can
only shrink. Every runtime currently offers every option above.
